claim: The CMP 170HX retains the full GA100 HBM2e memory bus, measuring ~1355 GB/s in clpeak, essentially identical to the A100.
stance_target: The repo's premise that the box has A100-class memory bandwidth (~1500 GB/s theoretical) despite being a mining SKU
scope_conditions: Single stock CMP 170HX, clpeak float8/float16 kernels, Linux, 2023
quoted_support: Global memory bandwidth (GBPS) float : 1165.79 float2 : 1269.69 float4 : 1343.50 float8 : 1355.40 float16 : 1350.14

claim: FP32 FMA/MAD throughput on the stock CMP 170HX is throttled to 394 GFLOPS, roughly 1/32 of the silicon's 12.6 TFLOPS theoretical FP32.
stance_target: The claim that the card is deliberately crippled for general compute, which is why an unlock/patch is needed before training is viable
quoted_support: tests show heavy performance restrictions on FMA and MAD floating-point operations, with a FP32 FMA speed of 394 GFLOPS and a FP64 FMA speed of 182 GFLOPS. The FP32 FMA performance is 1/100 of today's high-end GPUs.

claim: FP16 throughput on the stock card is ~42 TFLOPS and is unaffected by whether FMA is enabled or disabled.
stance_target: Whether bf16/fp16 training throughput on this card is limited by the FMA throttle
scope_conditions: mixbench SYCL build, stock card, no tensor-core path exercised
quoted_support: According to mixbench, FP16 performance is around ~42 TFLOPS (41869 GFLOPS), a level similar to a recent-gen low-end GPU. The use of FMA or not doesn't seem to affect the outcome.

claim: Tensor Cores do not deliver a throughput advantage through standard cuBLAS FP32 paths on the stock card: gpu_burn with CUBLAS_TENSOR_OP_MATH reaches only 6.2 TFLOPS, matching non-FMA FP32.
stance_target: The assumption that a stock CMP 170HX can reach A100-class bf16 tensor-core throughput (~162 TFLOPS/GPU as measured on the repo's unlocked box)
scope_conditions: gpu_burn -tc with CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_16F, stock card, single test
quoted_support: Since the performance is the same as standard non-FMA FP32 throughput as I previously showed, I have to conclude that the Tensor Cores probably aren't working or at least not useful.

claim: PCIe bandwidth on the stock card is locked to Gen1 x4, measured at 0.85 GB/s host-to-device.
stance_target: The repo's claim that the stock driver trains the cards at PCIe Gen1 and that all traffic crosses a very slow link
scope_conditions: Stock card, clpeak transfer benchmarks, single GPU
quoted_support: CMP 170HX's PCIe bandwidth is restricted to PCIe 1.0 x4, at 0.85 GB/s. Thus, if the application performs frequent data exchanges between CPU and GPU, or between different GPUs, it would be too slow to be acceptable

claim: The PCIe lockdown has two independent layers: an on-chip fuse pinning the device to Gen1, and a board-level x4 limit created by omitting AC-coupling capacitors on the extra lanes.
stance_target: The repo's distinction between a software Gen2 patch and a hardware width mod, and its claim that Gen3 is fuse-blocked
scope_conditions: lspci -vv and nvidia-smi link reporting on a stock card
quoted_support: There are in fact two layers of PCIe bandwidth lockdown. The first layer is the on-chip fuse, hardware or VBIOS lockdown (who knows) to PCIe Gen 1. The next is the circuit board level lockdown to x4 from x16 by omitting the AC coupling capacitors on some PCIe lanes to force a link degradation.

claim: The device reports a maximum PCIe generation of 2 while the host side supports Gen3, so Gen2 is a device-side fuse limit rather than a slot limit.
stance_target: The repo's claim that a link patch lifts the cards to Gen2 and that Gen3 is fuse-blocked (OPT_DISABLE_GEN3_SPEED)
scope_conditions: nvidia-smi GPU Link Info on a stock card in a Gen3-capable host
quoted_support: PCIe Generation Max : 2 Current : 1 Device Current : 1 Device Max : 1 Host Max : 3

claim: There is no NVLink on the CMP 170HX: the gold fingers exist on the A100-derived PCB but all NVLink components are unpopulated.
quoted_support: because the CMP 170HX uses the same Nvidia A100 circuit board, the gold fingers of the NV-Link interface exist, but the feature is unsupported with all components unpopulated on the PCB.

claim: Stock VRAM is restricted to 8 GiB and Resizable BAR is unavailable, with a largest BAR of 64 MiB.
stance_target: The repo's claim that 64 GB per card requires a community unlock rather than being a stock capability
scope_conditions: Stock card, 2023, before the cmpunlocker VRAM unlock existed
quoted_support: Resizable BAR is unavailable, this capability is surprisingly reported, but the largest BAR size is 64 MiB.

claim: Power draw is workload-class dependent: FMA-locked FP32/FP64 workloads draw only 60-75 W, while integer or memory-streaming workloads reach 160-180 W against a 250 W TDP.
stance_target: The repo's PWRBRK# / power-brake diagnostic, by showing that low observed power can reflect the FMA lockdown rather than a platform brake
scope_conditions: nvidia-smi power readings under gpu_burn, hashcat, STREAM-like and FluidX3D workloads
quoted_support: The power consumption of gpu_burn for FP32 and FP64 is around 60 watts. When running mixed-precision FP32/FP16 workloads ... the power consumption is around 75 watts with spikes to 100+ watts. ... A typical integer workload such as a password cracker like hashcat can push the power consumption to 160+ watts.

claim: VBIOS modification cannot bypass the performance locks because Nvidia enforces digital signature checks on all recent GPUs.
stance_target: The claim that the only viable unlock route is a patched kernel driver (cmpunlocker) rather than firmware modification
quoted_support: Unfortunately, all Nvidia GPUs since recent years have VBIOS digital signature checks, making VBIOS modification impossible. A few months ago, a bypass was found for RTX 20-series "Turing" based GPUs, unfortunately, it does not apply to Ampere GPUs.

claim: The card's PCB is near-identical to the A100 40 GB PCIe board, so A100 cooling and hardware mods transfer directly.
stance_target: Whether A100-class thermal solutions and A100-derived specifications can be assumed for this card
scope_conditions: Physical teardown compared against leaked A100 reference schematics
quoted_support: The Nvidia CMP 170HX uses a circuit board nearly - if not completely - identical to the Nvidia A100 (40 GiB). The only difference is the model number of the GPU ASIC GA100-105F-A1 which seems to be a cut-down version of the full GA100.
